sentences.text:
The petitioner has filed this present petition under Article 227 of the Constitution of India challenging the order dated 05.09.2024 passed in MACC No. 01/2023 passed by VI MACT,
Shajapur, whereby the petitioner/ company has filed application under Order 6 Rule 17 of CPC for amendment in reply regarding fake policy, but the learned tribunal has not accepted the plea of the petitioner and dismissed the application.
2. The brief facts of the case are that Respondent No. 1 to 4 have filed a Claim Petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, before the V Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Shajapur for compensation with the pleadings that the Respondent No. 6 Liendra driven Tractor No. MP41-AD- 4355 rashly and negligently, dashed Prahladsingh who was going on feet, due to which he died.

entities.text: V Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Shajapur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
On being notice,
the Petitioner Insurance Company filed its reply and thereby denied the averments of Claim Petition and prayed to dismiss the same.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:35692 2 MP-6162-2024 3.
After framing the issues the Respondent No. 1 has examined his witnesses, thereafter, the matter was listed for Non-Applicant evidence.
Petitioner has taken the plea that the Policy of the offending vehicle is totally fake.

This fact was came when the Petitioner Company has investigated in their official record and they got that no policy was issued in respect of the offending vehicle from the Petitioner Company and also not taken any premium in respect of the offending vehicle by the Petitioner Company.

4. Thereafter, the petitioner/ company has filed application under Order 6 Rule 17 of CPC for Sbi General Insurance Co.Ltd. vs Smt. Ranu on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19472839/

sentences.text: Hence, this petition before this Court.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the Tribunal has committed grave error in rejecting the amendment application without assigning proper reasons.
The amendment is necessary for adjudicating the real controversy and for enabling the petitioner to prove its defence of a fake policy.
Counsel further submits that unless the amendment is allowed, the petitioner would be deprived of raising a fundamental defence, which may result in miscarriage of justice.
Heard the petitioner and perused the record.
6. The law relating to amendments under Order VI Rule 17 CPC is well settled.
Amendments necessary for determining the real questions in controversy must be liberally allowed, unless they cause irreparable prejudice or fundamentally alter the nature of the case.
The plea regarding the policy being fake goes to the root of the Insurance Company's liability.

NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:35692 3 MP-6162-2024 Denying the Insurance Company an opportunity to take this defence, particularly when the case has not yet concluded,
would result in injustice.
The Tribunal, while dismissing the application, has not assigned any sufficient, cogent, or legally sustainable reasoning.
Therefore, the impugned order suffers from non-application of mind and is liable to be set aside.
7. The order dated 05.09.2024 passed by the learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal is set aside.
The application filed by the petitioner- Insurance Company under Order VI Rule 17 CPC dated 15.05.2024 is hereby allowed.
The Tribunal is directed to take the amended reply on record.
The respondents/claimants shall be afforded opportunity to file response and lead rebuttal evidence, if they desire.
The Tribunal shall thereafter proceed with the matter expeditiously and conclude the trial at the earliest without unnecessary delay.

8. With the aforesaid, petition stands disposed of.
(ALOK AWASTHI) JUDGE Vatan Sbi General Insurance Co.Ltd. vs Smt. Ranu on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19472839/
